bug_semantics: CVE-2020-36849 / GHSA-p27j-qf57-7cm7 is an unauthenticated arbitrary file upload (CWE-434) in the third-party WordPress plugin AIT CSV import/export (<= 3.0.3). The unauthenticated endpoint wp-content/plugins/ait-csv-import-export/admin/upload-handler.php accepts a multipart file without type/content validation and writes it under wp-content/uploads/, which can be executed as PHP. That sink is not present in rapid7/metasploit-framework. The assigned repo only contains a Metasploit exploit module (modules/exploits/multi/http/wp_ait_csv_rce.rb) that POSTs a PHP payload to the plugin handler and then requests the uploaded file; it is an offensive client for the plugin bug, not a vulnerability in Metasploit.
flaw_origin: This catalog row is a false positive for rapid7/metasploit-framework. Wordfence CNA record on CVE.org is PUBLISHED (not withdrawn/rejected) and names vendor AIT Themes / product AIT CSV import/export, versions <= 3.0.3. GHSA and NVD list the Metasploit module blob/raw URLs as references, which caused GitHub Advisory Database to attach the advisory to this repository. The module was added as a human-authored exploit (first commit d8c55501a52ece2e7360032c7422f95e2e595135, author h00die, subject ait csv improter exploit) and later only received CheckCode/CVE-id/rubocop/reliability edits. There is no Metasploit code path that implements the WordPress upload-handler or that is itself the CWE-434 issue.
ai_marker: absent; no BIC in rapid7/metasploit-framework because the advisory does not describe a vulnerability in this repository

This is not a security issue in Metasploit; the advisory-to-repo mapping is a false positive.
reasoning: Vulnerability-first: the CWE-434 sink is the WordPress plugin upload-handler.php, not any Metasploit Ruby module. The assigned repository is an exploit framework that ships a client for that third-party bug. A BIC search in rapid7/metasploit-framework would at best find the first-write of the exploit module, which does not introduce the advisory mechanism. AI attribution is therefore not applicable. Because the GHSA/CVE pair does not describe a vulnerability in the assigned repo, the correct closed judgment is FALSE_POSITIVE (misattributed advisory), not NOT_AI.
